description: Imports Zendesk Support helpdesk data (tickets and their audits/comments/metrics/side conversations, users, organizations, help center posts and articles, Talk calls, audit logs and account configuration objects) from a Zendesk instance.

placeholders.subdomain: the `subdomain` endpoint config field supplied by the user; validated against ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,62}$

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment `/api/v2` in the base URL

continuity.notes: Pure HTTP polling. The connector creates no server-side object in the customer's Zendesk instance; all resumption state (a datetime log cursor, or an opaque base64 incremental-export cursor for tickets/users and their children) is held by Flow. Nothing accrues on the customer's side while paused. The code contains no cursor-expiry handling, so no `ourSideLoss` is asserted; see `abstained`.

authTierRationale: The easiest offered mode is 'Email & API Token': the user pastes their Zendesk login email plus a self-serve API token generated in Zendesk admin, and the CDK's TokenSource sends them as HTTP Basic (the connector appends '/token' to the email, which is Zendesk's documented API-token Basic form). No app registration. The two OAuth modes are harder: both require the user's own Zendesk OAuth client id + secret (T2), and the current rotating mode additionally persists a refresh token plus access token and expiry (T3). Estuary's hosted control plane can run the authorization-code flow on the user's behalf via OAUTH2_SPEC, but standalone those modes are T2/T3.

unionMisfits.description: The Talk incremental export has no end-of-stream envelope flag. The loop terminates when the cursor it is about to send back equals the one it just sent (response end_time == request start_time). None of envelope_flag / short_page / absent_token / explicit_total describes 'the returned token is unchanged', so terminateOn is left null.

Time-based incremental exports are a hybrid: the pagination token IS the incremental watermark (a unix-second end_time echoed back as the next start_time), so `paginator` and `incrementalParam` name the same parameter and pages deliberately overlap by at least one record. A pure 'cursor' classification loses the fact that the token is a timestamp, is inclusive, and that the connector raises a hard error when >=1000 records share an updated_at (unadvanceable cursor).

The incremental cursor export's page size is adaptive rather than fixed: requests start at per_page=1000 and halve on each HTTP 504 'upstream request timeout' down to 1. `pageSize` records only the starting value. The cursor is also base64-decoded before being checkpointed and re-encoded before being sent.

proposedShape.tokenEncoding: base64 on the wire, decoded in state

unionMisfits.description: Eleven cursor-paginated and two page-paginated streams have NO server-side incremental parameter at all: every sweep re-reads the entire collection and the connector discards records whose updated_at is not greater than the log cursor. They are genuinely incremental from Flow's perspective but full-scan at the API. `incrementalParam: null` on an `incremental` PullSpec understates the cost.

Parent-driven streams: their log cursor is the PARENT stream's cursor (the tickets incremental-export cursor, or the posts updated_at watermark), not any field of the emitted record. There is no single PullSpec — each sweep is a parent pull plus one child pull per parent id, with the checkpoint taken at parent-page boundaries. The `pathPlaceholders` field carries this, but the two-request-family structure and the cursor's provenance do not fit.

ticket_metrics is not its own endpoint. It calls the tickets incremental cursor export with `include=metric_sets` and emits the sideloaded `metric_set` sub-object of each ticket, dropping tickets that have none. `recordsPath` is expressed as '/tickets/*/metric_set' but that is a projection out of the parent record, not an envelope path.

Windowed rather than watermark-driven: each sweep requests a closed [start_time, end_time] window capped at 30 days and advances the cursor to the window end regardless of what came back, so the cursor is wall-clock, not record-derived. Two query params jointly form the incremental filter; `incrementalParam` holds only one.

Which streams exist is decided at discover time by four live HTTP capability probes (Enterprise plan, Help Center, Talk, side conversations). The list is neither purely static nor discovered from a customer schema; `streamMode: static` plus a `discovery` block describing subtraction is the closest fit.

Per-binding intervals are connector-supplied defaults on ResourceConfig.interval that the user may override in the binding config; they are not fixed schedules. The Schedule union cannot express 'default, user-overridable'.

paginator.export_cursor.snippet:
next_page_cursor, end_of_stream = remainder.after_cursor, remainder.end_of_stream
if end_of_stream: return
params["cursor"] = next_page_cursor

paginator.talk_export.snippet:
if params["start_time"] == remainder.end_time:
    ...
    return
params["start_time"] = remainder.end_time

paginator.next_url.snippet:
while url:
    response = SideConversationsResponse.model_validate_json(await http.request(log, url))
    ...
    url = response.next_page

abstained.streams[?name=calls].pull.incremental.pa: The Talk incremental export carries no end_of_stream flag; the loop stops when the echoed end_time equals the start_time just sent. No member of the terminateOn enum expresses 'token unchanged', and picking envelope_flag or absent_token would be wrong. See unionMisfits.
abstained.streams[?name=call_legs].pull.incrementa: Same as calls: termination is 'returned cursor equals sent cursor', which the terminateOn enum cannot express.
abstained.streams[?name=tickets].cursorField: The checkpoint is an opaque base64 incremental-export cursor string (or, on first run, a stringified unix timestamp), not a document field. No record field is compared.
abstained.streams[?name=users].cursorField: Same opaque incremental-export cursor as tickets.
abstained.streams[?name=ticket_metrics].cursorFiel: Inherits the tickets incremental-export cursor; no field of the emitted metric_set is used for ordering.
abstained.streams[?name=ticket_audits].cursorField: Parent-driven: the checkpoint is the tickets export cursor taken at parent-page boundaries, not a field of the audit record.
abstained.streams[?name=post_votes].cursorField: The log cursor advances on the parent post's updated_at; the vote records themselves are read whole per post and carry no cursor field the connector inspects.
abstained.streams[?name=post_comments].cursorField: Same as post_votes: cursor lives on the parent post.
abstained.streams[?name=post_comment_votes].cursor: Two levels of parent (post -> comment); the cursor is the post updated_at watermark.
abstained.streams[?name=satisfaction_ratings].curs: The cursor is a wall-clock window end (min(now-61s, cursor+30d)), advanced whether or not records were returned; no record field is read.
abstained.streams[?name=account_attributes].pull.s: The offset-paginated snapshots expose no total count; only the presence/absence of next_page is used, so explicit_total termination was not asserted.
abstained.execution.continuity.ourSideLoss: Nothing in the connector or CDK handles an expired or invalidated Zendesk incremental-export cursor, and no retention window is referenced. Whether Zendesk itself invalidates old cursors is not determinable from this source.
abstained.execution.continuity.releasedOnShutdown: Not applicable/undeterminable: the connector creates no server-side artifact to release, so the field is left null rather than asserted true.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No default headers are set on the session; only the Authorization header injected by the CDK TokenSource.
abstained.streams[?name=organizations].pull.backfi: The time-based export sends no per_page; the 1,000-record page size is an observed server behaviour the code only reacts to (it raises if >=1000 records share an updated_at), never requests.
abstained.configFields[?name=credentials.username]: Marked non-secret because BasicAuth.username carries no secret annotation in the CDK, though it is half of a Basic credential pair.
abstained.streams[].supportedSyncModes.full_refres: Reported as supported for every incremental stream because Flow can always re-backfill a binding; the connector does not itself expose a per-stream mode toggle.
